name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
principle: The product writes, returns, logs, stores, or reveals sensitive information across a boundary to an actor that is not explicitly authorized. This is dangerous because confidentiality is lost and the data can enable privacy harm, credential theft, reconnaissance, or follow-on attacks.
detection_signals: HTTP response writes sensitive variables: password, passwd, token, secret, apiKey, ssn, creditCard, healthRecord, location
catch block sends exception details to client: e.printStackTrace(response.getWriter()), res.sendError(..., e.getMessage()), return stackTrace
logging call includes sensitive data: log.*, printf, System.out.println, NSLog, console.log with password/token/session/cookie/query/user object
debug-gated client output: if (debug) response.write(...), debugEnabled prints account, path, config, headers, environment
authentication response distinguishes states: "user not found" vs "bad password", different status codes, different timing paths
API returns full entity/object serialization: return user, JSON.stringify(user), ObjectMapper.writeValue(user) including private fields
externally reachable file/cache contains secrets: public/static/uploads/debug.log, .env, config.properties, core dump, backup file
negative_signals: authorization check immediately dominates sensitive output: if (!canViewSensitive(user, subject)) return 403
response DTO allowlists non-sensitive fields only: UserPublicDto(id,name), @JsonIgnore on password/token/ssn
sensitive fields are masked/redacted before sink: redact(token), maskCard(card), logSafe(user)
client-facing error is constant and generic: return "Invalid username or password"; internal stack trace logged only to restricted log
debug output compiled out or blocked in production: #ifndef NDEBUG, assert !isProduction(), debug endpoint requires admin role
logs are structured with denylisted/allowlisted fields and no raw object toString() or full request dump
false_defense_traps: Only hiding field names while still returning values or raw objects
Relying on HTTPS while sending secrets to an unauthorized user
Debug output protected only by a request parameter, cookie, or client-side flag
Logging full objects because toString()/JSON serialization seems harmless
Different error text, status code, or timing that still allows user/account enumeration
verification_focus: Does code explicitly manage, transmit, store, cleanse, or expose sensitive information in a way an unauthorized actor can observe?

consequence_chains.trigger: exception message or stack trace is returned to the client
consequence_chains.consequence: attacker reads paths, configuration names, SQL details, or internal state

consequence_chains.trigger: externally visible response, status, or timing differs for secret-dependent states
consequence_chains.consequence: attacker infers valid users, records, or internal decisions

consequence_chains.trigger: exposed table names, column names, or SQL text guide payload construction

patch_principle: Define trust boundaries and never send sensitive data outside the authorized boundary.
Return minimal allowlisted fields; use separate public DTOs instead of serializing internal objects.
Use generic client errors; keep detailed diagnostics only in access-controlled internal logs.
Redact or omit secrets from logs, debug output, files, caches, and telemetry.
Remove production debug output and enforce least privilege for data collection and access.
